{-# LANGUAGE BangPatterns #-}
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}

-- | Probe the current public source API and its default typed-run route.
module Main (main) where

import Control.Monad (when)
import Data.CFTA.Constraint (Constraint)
import qualified Data.CFTA.Enumeration as E
import Data.CFTA.Gen.Synthesis
    ( Encoding (FirstOrder)
    , Library (..)
    , Program (..)
    , Query (..)
    , Space (..)
    , Type (..)
    , rawSearchSpace
    , reduceWithOrder
    , renderProgram
    , solutionsOfSize
    , (~>)
    )
import Data.CFTA.Symbol (Symbol, symbolText)
import Data.CFTA.Term (Term)
import qualified Data.CFTA.Term as Term
import Data.Text (Text)
import System.Environment (getArgs)
import System.Exit (die)
import System.IO (BufferMode (LineBuffering), hFlush, hSetBuffering, stdout)

-- | A source AST and its independent finite-HM membership expectation.
data Candidate = Candidate
    { candidateName :: String
    , candidateProgram :: Program
    , finiteHMExpected :: Bool
    }

-- | One library, query, source size, and finite list of candidate ASTs.
data ProbeCase = ProbeCase
    { caseName :: String
    , caseLibrary :: Library
    , caseQuery :: Query
    , caseSize :: Int
    , caseCandidates :: [Candidate]
    }

-- | The observed prefix count, exhaustion flag, and matched candidate ASTs.
data Summary = Summary !Integer !Bool [Program]

-- | Build singleton component groups with the ordinary first-order encoding.
mkLibrary :: [(Text, Type)] -> Library
mkLibrary entries = Library [(name, typ, [name]) | (name, typ) <- entries] [] [] FirstOrder

-- | Select one of the three source-generated cases.
lookupCase :: String -> Maybe ProbeCase
lookupCase name = case name of
    "BOUND" -> Just $ ProbeCase name boundLibrary boundQuery 3
        [Candidate "bound_self_application" (App (Var "sink") (App (Var "bound") (Var "bound"))) False]
    "SKI" -> Just $ ProbeCase name skiLibrary (Query [] bool) 4
        [ Candidate "ski_self_application" (App (Var "sink") (App (App (Var "s") (Var "i")) (Var "i"))) False
        , Candidate "ski_finite_control" (App (Var "sink") (App (App (Var "s") (Var "k")) (Var "k"))) True
        ]
    "POLY" -> Just $ ProbeCase name (mkLibrary [("i", a ~> a)]) (Query [] (bool ~> bool)) 2
        [Candidate "polymorphic_identity_control" (App (Var "i") (Var "i")) True]
    _ -> Nothing
  where
    a = TVar "a"
    b = TVar "b"
    c = TVar "c"
    bool = TCons "Bool" []
    sinkType = a ~> bool
    boundLibrary = mkLibrary [("sink", sinkType)]
    boundQuery = Query [("bound", a ~> b)] bool
    skiLibrary = mkLibrary
        [ ("sink", sinkType)
        , ("s", (a ~> b ~> c) ~> (a ~> b) ~> a ~> c)
        , ("i", a ~> a)
        , ("k", a ~> b ~> a)
        ]

-- | Decode exactly as Synthesis.toProgram at source lines 963-966.
-- This function only observes the typed run. It does not run enumeration.
programOfTypedTerm :: Term Symbol -> Program
programOfTypedTerm term = case (Term.rootLabel term, Term.subForest term) of
    ("app", [_, _, function, argument]) -> App (programOfTypedTerm function) (programOfTypedTerm argument)
    ("filter", [_, candidates]) -> programOfTypedTerm candidates
    (symbol, _) -> Var (symbolText symbol)

-- | Flush phase progress before source construction or enumeration starts.
progress :: String -> IO ()
progress message = putStrLn message >> hFlush stdout

-- | Print one bounded value and state whether its encoding is complete.
printBounded :: (Show a) => String -> a -> IO ()
printBounded label value = do
    let limit = 16384
        prefix = take (limit + 1) (show value)
    putStrLn $ label <> ".show_complete=" <> show (length prefix <= limit)
    putStrLn $ label <> "=" <> take limit prefix

-- | Scan each public program at most once. Retain only candidate ASTs.
scanPublic :: [Candidate] -> [Program] -> IO Summary
scanPublic candidates = go 0 []
  where
    go !count !found programs
        | all ((`elem` found) . candidateProgram) candidates = pure $ Summary count False found
        | otherwise = case programs of
            [] -> pure $ Summary count True found
            program : rest -> do
                let matching = filter ((== program) . candidateProgram) candidates
                    firstMatch = not (null matching) && program `notElem` found
                    !newFound = if firstMatch then program : found else found
                when firstMatch $ do
                    putStrLn $ "public.match=" <> show (map candidateName matching)
                    printBounded "public.ast" program
                    hFlush stdout
                go (count + 1) newFound rest

-- | Scan one default typed-run stream and retain its exact first matched pairs.
-- At most one pair per candidate is printed. Oversized output is marked.
scanTyped :: [Candidate] -> [(Term Symbol, [(Constraint, Term Symbol)])] -> IO Summary
scanTyped candidates = go 0 []
  where
    go !count !found runs
        | all ((`elem` found) . candidateProgram) candidates = pure $ Summary count False found
        | otherwise = case runs of
            [] -> pure $ Summary count True found
            run@(term, _) : rest -> do
                let program = programOfTypedTerm term
                    matching = filter ((== program) . candidateProgram) candidates
                    firstMatch = not (null matching) && program `notElem` found
                    !newFound = if firstMatch then program : found else found
                when firstMatch $ do
                    putStrLn $ "typed.match=" <> show (map candidateName matching)
                    printBounded "typed.ast" program
                    printBounded "typed.same_run_term_and_residuals" run
                    hFlush stdout
                go (count + 1) newFound rest

-- | Report presence, or absence only after the observed stream is exhausted.
printSummary :: String -> [Candidate] -> Summary -> IO ()
printSummary phase candidates (Summary count exhausted found) = do
    putStrLn $ phase <> ".scanned=" <> show count
    putStrLn $ phase <> ".exhausted=" <> show exhausted
    mapM_ report candidates
    hFlush stdout
  where
    report candidate = do
        let present = candidateProgram candidate `elem` found
            status
                | present = "present"
                | exhausted = "absent_after_exhaustion"
                | otherwise = "unobserved"
        putStrLn $ phase <> ".candidate=" <> show (candidateName candidate)
            <> " status=" <> status
            <> " finite_hm_expected=" <> show (finiteHMExpected candidate)

-- | Evaluate the public and diagnostic routes once each, as separate runs.
runCase :: ProbeCase -> IO ()
runCase config = do
    progress $ "case=" <> caseName config
    putStrLn $ "source_size=" <> show (caseSize config)
    printBounded "library" (caseLibrary config)
    printBounded "query" (caseQuery config)
    mapM_ (printBounded "candidate.ast" . candidateProgram) (caseCandidates config)
    mapM_ (printBounded "candidate.source" . renderProgram . candidateProgram) (caseCandidates config)
    progress "phase=public.solutionsOfSize.begin"
    publicSummary <- scanPublic (caseCandidates config) $
        solutionsOfSize (caseLibrary config) (caseQuery config) (caseSize config)
    printSummary "public" (caseCandidates config) publicSummary
    progress "phase=typed.default.begin; evaluation=separate_from_public"
    let space = reduceWithOrder $ rawSearchSpace (caseLibrary config) (caseQuery config) (caseSize config)
    printBounded "typed.reduced_root_reachesConstrainedMu" (E.reachesConstrainedMu (spaceNode space))
    progress "phase=typed.default.root_ready"
    typedSummary <- scanTyped (caseCandidates config) $
        E.runsBy (spaceOrder space) "Mu" (spaceNode space)
    printSummary "typed" (caseCandidates config) typedSummary
    progress "case_complete=True; observations_only=True; partial_type_scope=retained"

-- | Run exactly one named case in this process.
main :: IO ()
main = do
    hSetBuffering stdout LineBuffering
    args <- getArgs
    case args of
        [name] | Just config <- lookupCase name -> runCase config
        _ -> die "Usage: probe BOUND|SKI|POLY"

-- | Ordinary finite-type Haskell controls. This module does not import CFTA.
module Good where

-- | The ordinary S combinator.
s :: (a -> b -> c) -> (a -> b) -> a -> c
s f g x = f x (g x)

-- | The polymorphic identity.
i :: a -> a
i x = x

-- | The ordinary K combinator.
k :: a -> b -> a
k x _ = x

-- | Discard a value of any monotype.
sink :: a -> Bool
sink _ = True

-- | SKK has a finite type. Instantiate its argument type to Bool.
goodSKI :: Bool
goodSKI = sink (s k k :: Bool -> Bool)

-- | Two uses of polymorphic identity have separate finite instances.
goodPoly :: Bool -> Bool
goodPoly = i i

-- | Expected ordinary GHC type error: SII requires an infinite type.
module BadSKI where

import Good (i, s, sink)

-- | SII cannot have a finite ordinary Haskell type.
badSKI :: Bool
badSKI = sink (s i i)

-- | Expected ordinary GHC type error: the same bound variable applies to itself.
module BadBound where

import Good (sink)

-- | The query gives bound one rigid monomorphic function type.
badBound :: (a -> b) -> Bool
badBound bound = sink (bound bound)

constrained_mu_source_audit.text:
# FirstOrder source roots and the constrained-recursion flag

Status: bounded read-only audit. No positive source witness was established.
No compilation, runtime probe, test, source change, or cache experiment was run.
No conclusion about every reduced root is claimed.

## Existing source restriction

`cfta-generator/src/Data/CFTA/Gen/Synthesis.hs:131-135` represents a finite parsed
Type by TVar, TFun, and TCons. Library/Query contain these Types, not user-provided
CFTA nodes (`Library:230-244`). This is the finite parsed input domain; arbitrary
Haskell cyclic values or bottoms are not a separate source encoding.

For FirstOrder, `typesOf:841-843` selects `allTypes`. Its one recursive definition
at475-482 contains arrows, four variable leaves, and constructor rows. All these
edges have no constraints. The other createMu site, at490, belongs to Curried
encoding. It is not a FirstOrder example.

`typeNode:416-420` builds finite rigid Types. `generalize:525-532` replaces source
variables by allTypes and adds repeated-variable equalities to the finite outer
ordinary row. `rawSearchSpace:779-839` builds finite Program rows with application
and goal-filter equalities. None of those source definitions writes a constraint
inside the recursive allTypes body. Source names and reserved markers are not
needed to obtain this structural restriction.

The checked Lean law is exact and already exists:
`lean/MicroCFTA/SourceSynthesisCurrentSourceGuards.lean:320-323`,
`firstOrderRaw_guards_plainMu`, derives `PlainMu top expression` for every actual
successful CURRENT FirstOrder construction, with arbitrary source inputs/avoid rules.
`SourceSynthesisRecursiveOrigins.lean:23-37` defines PlainMu: every binder body
has only Top guards; finite ordinary ancestors may have equality guards.
`allTypes_plainMu:118`, `generalize_plainMu:189`, and the final current law cover
the source operations. No additional input freshness or provider gate is involved.

Thus there is a source-based reason to expect a raw FirstOrder root to have
`reachesConstrainedMu = False`. This is not a theorem of the Haskell Boolean
implementation: the syntax/build/Boolean correspondence is a separate bridge.

## Why this does not yet settle the DEFAULT reduced root

`Synthesis.hs:671-683` applies up to30 rounds of
`withoutRedundantEdges . reducePartially`. `orderedSearchSpace:774-775` then uses
`reduceWithOrder`; `orderedSpace:724-729` applies `refoldEdges` to the final round.
The flag is set from THAT reached root by `Enumeration.hs:296-311`.

`Enumeration.hs:545-561` checks whether a reachable Mu has ANY equality/residual
constraint in its body. Ordinary constrained ancestors alone do not make the
flag True. This distinction explains why a polymorphic Program or a graph with
many ordinary equalities need not exercise the flag-positive branch.

`cfta/src/Data/CFTA/Equality/Operations.hs:83-86` leaves an encountered Mu unchanged.
However, `reduceEqConstraints:216-239` also forms intersections at equality paths.
`requireAll:292-303` and `editAll:328-334` can expose Mu rows at finite paths.
`cfta/src/Data/CFTA/Interned/Operations.hs:504-508,544-552` can create a new Mu
through `intersectOpen`/`maybeMu`; the recursive reference must actually recur.
`refold:191-203`/`refoldEdges:211-226` replace exact existing unfoldings by binders.
These operations require a preservation argument, not only the source restriction.

The existing `SourceSynthesisRecursiveOrigins.lean:5-11` documentation explicitly
limits PlainMu to constructor instructions and excludes a preservation claim for
native normalization, projection, intersection, and enumeration. I did not find
an existing closure law that proves the Haskell reduced/refolded Boolean is False.

## Exact remaining question, with no future gate

For finite parsed FirstOrder Library/Query inputs and the actual successful
source size, the candidate source-only claim is:

    not (reachesConstrainedMu
      (spaceNode (orderedSearchSpace lib query size)))

This remains UNPROVED. A route must establish the raw/build correspondence and
preservation of equality-free recursive bodies through the actual bounded reduction
and refolding, including newly created intersection binders. Merely observing
`go _ (Mu n) = Mu n` is insufficient. If this closure holds, the default FirstOrder
flag-positive path is unreachable, although generic CFTA enumeration still needs it.

## Search result and limit

The inspected actual source examples were `SynthesisSpec.hs` (FirstOrder cases and
historyQueries), its Hybrid/States/Liquid companion references, the component-
synthesis README section, and Synthesis construction/reduction definitions.
No example there asserts `reachesConstrainedMu` True for an actual FirstOrder root.
The positive constrained-Mu cases found in `cfta/test/Data/CFTA/EqualitySpec.hs`
(461,488,512,543,757) construct CFTA nodes directly. They do not satisfy this task's
source-API requirement and are not proposed as runtime cases. No new run is proposed
until review. The three earlier runtime roots are Root's evidence, not a proof of
this general negative property. No Haskell defect or counterexample is established.
